guide.title: Explanations and deletion propagation
guide.summary: PROV-001's retained provenance specialized without recomputing derivations: the exact effect of deleting or re-valuing source tuples on every answer's existence and multiplicity, propagated incrementally through the DAG by the semirings' update laws (CUDA: one work item per change set); lineage, relevant, counterfactual and minimal sufficient sources and why-not restorations relative to a base; answer probabilities under independent tuples, exact on the DAG with its shared variables through COUNT-002's decision diagrams, or certified bounds past the budget, never products of per-derivation probabilities.

PROV-002.cpu: Native C (math_explain.c; the propagation tr_expl_set and its update laws inline in math_explain.h): an immutable explanation state copied from a PROV-001 plan's cone (nothing re-derived from the sources) with reverse edges (one parent entry per child entry), the answers of every node, the cone node of every variable and the baseline under a declared base valuation (N multiplicities in unsigned 128 bits and B existence with PROV-001's shared evaluators, and the per-node support counts B needs); deletion propagation of change sets (deletions, restorations, multiplicities) visiting only the nodes above the changed tuples in increasing order through a min-heap with an early cutoff, PLUS by the linear law (old N minus the changed children's old values plus their new ones), TIMES by the product of the children's new values (DELTA-002's finite difference dA B + A dB + dA dB), B by counting maintenance of the true (OR) or false (AND) children, with per set every answer's N and B, an overflow status redone in B alone, the nodes recomputed and the answers changed; explanations relative to the base on COUNT-002's decision diagram of the answer's monotone lineage (absent sources FALSE for why, present ones TRUE for why-not): the lineage, the relevant sources (the support of the existence function), the counterfactual sources, the minimal sufficient sets (minimal models on the diagram, refused past max_sets), a smallest sufficient set, the minimal why-not restorations, with found / absent / present / underivable status; answer probabilities under independent tuple probabilities as exact rationals (the weighted count of the lineage diagram with (p, 1 - p): shared variables exact) within the diagram budget, or certified outward-rounded bounds on the DAG without compilation (exact independence on variable-disjoint children, Harris-FKG bounds for increasing events otherwise).
PROV-002.gpu: CUDA kernel math_explain_gpu.cu: tr_mgpu_explain_propagate runs one work item per change set with the shared tr_expl_set on its own scratch row (the min-heap, the PLUS / TIMES / counting update laws, the early cutoff) and its own rows of answers, status, nodes recomputed and answers changed, restoring the touched scratch entries so rows are clean for the next launch chunk (chunks within 64 MiB of scratch); the host checks the view, the change sets and the budget first; equal to the CPU byte for byte. Exact probabilities can count the lineage diagram with COUNT-002's level kernels (tr_mgpu_symcount_levels).
budgets: State: circuit = cone nodes, support = child entries, output = answers, bytes = the copies, reverse edges, answer lists and baseline.
Propagation: output = change sets x answers, bytes = the scratch (65 per cone node; CUDA: every device copy, the outputs and the scratch chunk).

Lineage diagrams: COUNT-002's builder (circuit = nodes held, iterations = apply steps, bytes); necessary sources: iterations = levels x diagram nodes; minimal sets: support = the set entries held, output = max_sets (refused, never truncated); probability bounds: bytes = the support bitsets and intervals.
limitations: PROV-001's operators only (selection, union, equi-join, group-by; no aggregates other than multiplicities, no negation, outer joins or recursion); for a global group (always present) the existence explained and propagated is COUNT(*) > 0.

Probabilities assume independent source tuples; the exact path is bounded by the lineage diagram, whose size depends on the variable order (DFS first appearance by default); past it the bounds are certified but can be loose on heavily shared lineages.

Explanations and probability bounds are per answer and single-threaded on the CPU; minimal sets are enumerated explicitly from the diagram; propagation is batched on the device but each change set is sequential within its work item.
